SMTO-CTX-0010 — SMTO couldn't get a web page

GUID: db0fe2e6-7852-473c-ab51-843bce19a432
Slug: read-unavailable
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: context

What happened

  • SMTO tried to read a public web page for this task but couldn't get it. This error doesn't say whether the site couldn't be reached or the page couldn't be read.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the same web address in your own browser. Check that it loads and doesn't ask you to sign in. SMTO can only read public pages, so a missing, broken or sign-in page will fail every time.
  2. Make sure the computer running SMTO's server is connected to the internet. SMTO fetches pages from that computer, so a network problem there stops every web read.
  3. Ask SMTO to read the page one more time. If it fails again, attach the document with Add context or point SMTO to a different page. Reading a page changes nothing, so one more try is safe, and another source avoids a page SMTO can't read.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's reply includes information from the page or the source you gave it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the web address, to the person who manages SMTO so they can check the server's network. Don't keep resending the same request; choose another source instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The public webpage reader caught an unclassified exception while fetching or extracting a page and returned error_kind read_unavailable; whether the cause was access, network or text extraction is not recorded.

What this means

  • The public webpage reader caught an otherwise unclassified exception; its result does not establish whether the cause was access, transport or extraction. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The public webpage reader caught an otherwise unclassified exception; its result does not establish whether the cause was access, transport or extraction.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the source response and the retained read phase; distinguish access refusal from content extraction or transport failure.

How to fix it

  • Reproduce the fetch from the Server host (DNS, TLS, proxy, connection reset) and check the Server log around the read in skills/web/reader.py read_page. The reader marks this as retryable at most once; otherwise supply an alternative source the task is allowed to read.
  • Restore or reselect the authorized source within the owning task scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The same authorized source can be read and its result identifies the returned content and completeness.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
